title: Signature Constraint Loom
description: Higgins' constraint loom weaves constraints as threads on a visible frame: each thread's tension shows how tight the constraint is, and the woven solution is the cloth where all threads hold. Over-tight threads glow before they snap the weave.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
n=4
# Count n-queens solutions by backtracking with forward checking
def solve(n):
    sols=0
    cols=set(); d1=set(); d2=set()
    def bt(row):
        nonlocal sols
        if row==n: sols+=1; return
        for c in range(n):
            if c in cols or (row-c) in d1 or (row+c) in d2: continue
            cols.add(c); d1.add(row-c); d2.add(row+c)
            bt(row+1)
            cols.remove(c); d1.remove(row-c); d2.remove(row+c)
    bt(0); return sols
import time; t0=time.time(); s=solve(n); dt=time.time()-t0
print(f"n=4 solutions={s} time={dt:.3f}s")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Constraints register as threads with tension meters updated by propagation; the weaver lays solution threads across. Tension warnings fire before infeasibility, naming the tightest threads.
